text:
emma: Heads-up — around 09:12 UTC we saw a small spike (~0.7%) in envelope encryption failures. Appears related to key ARN mismatch between service cache and KMS.

kms-monitor-bot: Alert: 2026-03-20T09:12:03Z - KMS_MISMATCH_ERROR - service-frontend - 87 failures in 5m.

raj: Looking. Which KMS provider? AWS, GCP, or both?

emma: Mostly AWS KMS. A handful of GCP KMS errors too but different code path. Logs show callers using an outdated key ARN pulled from local ARN cache (we recently changed key rotation alias).

laura: Did we just push the RBAC/key alias change yesterday? I remember a rotation + alias swap for env-prod.

emma: Yes — rotation completed 03:00 UTC and we updated alias mapping in vault. Service A still had the old ARN in its in-memory cache (TTL was 24h). When it tried envelope-encrypt with old ARN, KMS returned InvalidKeyArn for some cross-account requests.

dave: Impact looks bounded — most requests retried and succeeded once cache refreshed or service restarted. No customer data exposed. Near-miss.

sophie: Any audit logs we can attach for the customer-facing incident review? Need KMS request IDs and audit trail.

emma: I grabbed a bundle: includes KMS request_ids, service headers, and the alias swap entry from the rotation runbook. Attaching to the incident ticket.

raj: Short term mitigations I propose: reduce ARN cache TTL from 24h -> 5m, add a listener to invalidate cache on alias-change webhook, and add an explicit fallback to resolve alias via KMS GetKeyId if envelope encrypt fails with InvalidKeyArn. Thoughts?

laura: +1 to all. Also add exponential backoff with jitter on initial attempts to prevent thundering restarts hitting KMS.

emma: We should also tighten RBAC rollout: when alias is switched, any service that reads alias should do a double-check read-through to KMS for 1 minute after rotation.

dave: Operational note: no need for immediate customer communication. We'll mark as "near-miss" in postmortem but keep internal follow-up.

kms-monitor-bot: Action created: ENGSEC-1592 - investigate ARN cache invalidation and mitigation. Assigned to raj.

raj: Will implement TTL change + invalidation hook this morning. Planning to ship a small patch to service A and service B, monitor for anomalies.

laura: I'll add a runtime guard so if envelope encrypt returns InvalidKeyArn, we try alias resolution and only escalate if that also fails. Keep the change feature-flagged.

emma: Quick log snippet:

```
2026-03-20T09:11:57Z ERROR service-frontend request_id=abc123 KMS=aws InvalidKeyArn KeyArn=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/old-key-uuid alias=alias/prod-main
2026-03-20T09:11:58Z WARN service-frontend cache_miss resolving alias alias/prod-main -> arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/new-key-uuid
2026-03-20T09:12:01Z INFO service-frontend request_id=abc124 KMS=aws Encrypt succeeded KeyArn=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/new-key-uuid
```

emma: Immediate action items: 1) raj change cache TTL + invalidation hook (ETA 2h). 2) laura add alias-resolve fallback (ETA end of day, feature-flagged). 3) emma prepare short postmortem (due EOD).

raj: Starting on 1) now. Will open PR and request quick review from laura.

laura: I can review and help test. We'll add metrics: InvalidKeyArn count, fallback-resolution success rate, and time-to-first-success after alias swap.

sophie: Add a compliance note: ensure audit entries include the pre-rotation ARN and the post-rotation ARN for traceability. Also record who triggered alias swap.

emma: Good call — I'll export the rotation job metadata and attach.

dave: Postmortem outline: timeline, root cause (cache TTL + alias swap without read-through), mitigations, and verification plan. Keep it short.

raj: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/1234 - change cache TTL to 5m + invalidate on webhook. Rolling this out to canary first.

laura: Deployed runtime guard to canary. Observability hooked. Will promote if metrics look green.

emma: Thanks all. No escalations for now. We should also review rotation runbook to include a verification step for in-flight services.

dave: Agree. I'll add a quick checklist item to the rotation runbook.

emma: Follow-up: postmortem draft in ticket ENGSEC-1592, tagging infra and runtime. I'll ping when ready for review. :white_check_mark:
